provenance.source: tr --version: "tr (GNU coreutils) 9.11" (the binary first on this host PATH, the same coreutils family the spec-help-drift check pins); tr --help synopsis "Usage: tr [OPTION]... STRING1 [STRING2]"; macOS /usr/bin/tr man tr(1) SYNOPSIS cross-checked 2026-10-25

stdin.source: tr --help: "Translate, squeeze, and/or delete characters from standard input, writing to standard output."; man tr(1) (macOS), DESCRIPTION: "The tr utility copies the standard input to the standard output with substitution or deletion of selected characters." Neither synopsis has a FILE operand, so stdin is always the input

stdout.source: tr --help: "...writing to standard output." The stream is the (filtered) input content, so stdout carries content

unknownFlag.source: tr --help lists exactly -c/-C/--complement, -d/--delete, -s/--squeeze-repeats, -t/--truncate-set1, --help, --version; man tr(1) (macOS) adds -u. No documented behavior for an unlisted flag, so the fail-closed default ("insufficient") applies; -u (BSD only) is deliberately unmodeled
